text: Second, the framework under the Compulsory Education Act does not extend to intervening in the event the parent neglects sending his or her child to primary school.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: What it does is to provide penal consequences.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: However, it does not directly address the plight of the child if the parent does not do the right thing.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Also, as mentioned by the hon Minister for Education (Schools) Mr Ng Chee Meng in this House before, the approach of MOE is not to charge the parents in Court but to counsel them to comply with the requirements.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Third, the future prospects of the child would be indelibly affected by reason of the parents' neglect in registering him for school and ensuring that he attends school regularly.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Whilst this is not physical harm, it is harm that is still debilitating in terms of the impact on his future.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In my respectful view, the Compulsory Education Act and the Children and Young Persons Act should complement each other so that the whole suite of options would be available to help the child if a parent neglects to send his or her child to school.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: After all, the parent would have committed a criminal offence by virtue of his conduct.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I am aware that we are not dealing with big numbers.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In my respectful view, though, even one case of a child being deprived of education is a case too many.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I am not advocating that the powers be exercised in every instance that a parent does not send his or her child to school.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: All I am asking is that the state be provided with the requisite powers so that it can intervene in an appropriate case.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Do a quick search on adult diapers in online marketplaces, and you will be inundated by the array of long-term care products and services listings.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: If we fast forward to 10 years, we will see more white-hair people around us.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: I will just be promoted to be a member in this group!

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: There is an increasing need for the younger population to plan ahead as they get older.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: But getting people to plan ahead earlier is an uphill one.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Often enough, they feel they are "too young" to have a situation where they have a chronic illness or to do retirement planning, and that the policy message is for someone else.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Also, there is a lack of recognition that many of the policies earmarked for the younger population are likely to have long-term consequences as they age, fertility rate, for instance.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: This is especially when the Government has limits to policy implementation.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: A classic example, I was just talking to a friend of mine.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: She is in her 40s and works in the healthcare sector.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Yet, she is totally impervious to the policy messages because she has other priorities to think about.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: We know what we should do, but actually doing it is another matter.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: As we all know, we are all good doctors but bad patients.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Good at dispensing advice but bad at heeding them.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: I just spoke of two different demographics – the elderly and the middle-aged.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: How is the Ministry working to reach out to these different groups?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: We will inevitably see, in time to come, that sales of incontinence products will outpace that of milk powder and baby diapers.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: How will the Ministry ensure that the elderly population is being cared for without curbing the well-being of its young?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: How do we balance the need to care for the older generation without neglecting the needs of the young?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Indeed, the demographic challenges we face are daunting, with falling birth rates and a rapidly ageing population.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: In light of these challenges, how is MSF working to meet the changing needs of Singaporeans and our families?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: The recent IPS survey asked if one is willing to pay higher taxes to fund higher social spending on the elderly or go tap the national Reserves.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Looking at the mixed bag of responses, there are almost equal differing responses.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: I came across this feature from Assoc Prof Tan En Ser, Department of Sociology at the National University of Singapore (NUS).

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: He postulates that in most Confucian societies, the basis of intergenerational support is filial piety, a value which prescribes that the adults have an obligation to support their parents if they are in need.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Nonetheless, filial piety is an often-socialised term in this country.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: So, many Singaporeans exhibit filial piety and believe this to be an important and enduring trait.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: However, this attribute is easier to fulfil if there is financial independence either on the part of the parents, or the children are there and able to support their parents comfortably.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: But our commitment to observe filial piety can be severely tested.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: We can be forced to a corner when we face difficulties upholding our end of the commitment.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: With the IPS study in mind, and without eroding the role of values or family as the first line of support, how does the Ministry see the role of the Government, social service sector and the community actively coming forward to help?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: How can the Ministry strengthen families, as well as the community, so that they are confident in providing care for the vulnerable among us?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Chairman, Sir, according to section 31 of the Mental Capacity Act, the Public Guardian has a total of 11 functions that are geared towards enabling and protecting persons who lack mental capacity.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: These functions include setting up and maintaining a register of Lasting Powers of Attorney (LPAs), setting up and maintaining a register of Court orders that appoint deputies, receiving reports from donees and deputies, and investigating any alleged violation of any provision in the Mental Capacity Act, including complaints about the way in which donees and deputies are exercising their powers.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Given the many onerous functions of the Public Guardian, I would like to find out how many staff work in the Office of Public Guardian (OPG) and whether there is enough manpower to handle the work.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Such delays might also have serious consequences, if the donor's mental state is fast deteriorating and he becomes mentally incapable while his LPA application is pending for registration by OPG.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I am concerned that if the function of registration is already backlogged, how does the OPG carry out the other more difficult functions, such as investigating alleged violations of the Act?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Does the Ministry know what the common reasons were for the donors to revoke their LPAs?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Do these reasons indicate that there is some lack of understanding of how the LPA works?

speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
text: As the Ministry looks into the matter of Eldercare Leave for caregivers who are also employed in full-time or part-time jobs, I would like to urge that they will also consider ways of providing assistance to those caregivers who are not.

speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
text: As of now, the burden of informal caregiving falls disproportionately on women.

speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
text: And our dependence on this group of Singaporeans is real.

speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
text: Eldercare Leave could well help relieve some of the pressure on informal caregivers who also work at other jobs, but almost half of our informal caregivers to seniors do not work at other jobs, often because of the unpaid caregiving responsibilities that they have taken on to their financial detriment and to their reduced retirement adequacy.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: As an Asian society, we believe in families as our first line of support.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Over the years, various studies done reaffirm this.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: For instance, in a study done by Kau Ah Keng et al, published in 2001 – a little bit dated – Singaporeans "strongly subscribed to the traditional value of supporting one's parents in their old age".

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: However, as our population changes with rapid ageing, smaller family sizes and more singles, the strength of family support is increasingly being tested.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: This will have profound implications on our social structure and how welfare is delivered.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: In a recent IPS study published in "Singapore Perspectives 2018 'Together'", one finding indicated that Singaporeans believe the Government ought to bear greater responsibility in taking care of older people in the absence of familial support, a shift from the "many helping hands" concept.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: But I wonder if it is also the beginning of a shift from our traditional value of family support.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Given these, I would like to ask MSF if indeed there has been a shift in family and social values and, if so, how will this impact Singapore in the long run.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Often, many of these senior citizens are uncomfortable seeking help from their children.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: They feel that their children have enough financial problems of their own without having to worry about their elderly parents.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I would refer these seniors to SSO and, usually, some form of assistance is given.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: There appears to be an increasing expectation that the Government ought to bear a large part of the responsibility of taking care of the elderly.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Is this reflected in the results of the recent IPS survey which Ms Tin Pei Ling also referred to?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: If families are facing some difficulties, as far as possible, there should be a support structure in place to assist.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: However, it is important that the family continues to be the first line of support for those who need help.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: This is a value that our society should embrace and adhere to.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Is there some way we could provide families with some support but ultimately empower them to care for their vulnerable family members themselves?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Chairman, MSF has committed to improving early childhood education outcomes through raising the quality of our educators and the centres' operations.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: In a tight labour market, how can the Ministry continue to grow the sector?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Raising the quality of early childhood education requires better staff and curriculum.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: This, in turn, necessarily incur higher manpower and operating costs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: However, our younger Singaporeans are already facing twin challenges because they are already having children later in life, they end up having to take care of the young children while caring for the elderly parents at the same time.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Such sandwich situation is expected to be more commonplace over time.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: This has somewhat eroded the support from the subsidies.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Can the Government review the subsidies, taking into consideration the twin challenges that our middle-income young parents face?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: How can we continue to ensure that early childhood education continues to be affordable or the quality improved?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: In conjunction with the review of the subsidies, we should also expand the market-moderating effect of anchor operators.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Beyond childcare, student care support is something that our parents will need readily as more families have both parents working.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: It has become as indispensable as childcare support.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: It is comforting to note that our lower-income families at the lowest income tier can pay as little as $5 per month.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: I hope that the Ministry can also similarly look into enhancing our student care support to include parents up to the 50th percentile income tier, so that our young parents can have similar support from preschool to primary school.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Next, I would like to discuss the issues surrounding caregivers taking care of our special needs, disabled and elderly residents.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Caregiving can be both physically and emotionally draining.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Often times, caregivers need some short time away to either recharge or run errands.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: However, respite care can be expensive, especially for lower-wage caregivers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Can the Ministry look into strengthening the provision of respite care with a view towards increasing the availability and reducing the costs of respite care?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Besides respite care, more caregivers would also need support in accessing the wide range of Government services and also mutual support from other caregivers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: A "one-stop centre" announced earlier last year was an important milestone.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Would the Minister provide an update on the new caregiver support centre and if more centres are planned for island-wide implementation?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Lastly, we have done much over the years to support our parents in helping to care for the special needs children under the Enabling Masterplan.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: One of the key concerns that many parents have is what happens to the children when they are old enough – 18 years old?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Most of them will have to leave the Special Education (SPED) schools and either go into open employment, sheltered employment or training development centres.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Would there be sufficient affordable places in these different pathways and day-care centres for them, such that they can continue with development?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: With sufficient capacity, we can give our parents, who have worked many years to provide care and support to their special needs children, the comfort knowing that they will continue to be taken of and to lead meaningful and abled lives.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Residents at the two new estates in Hougang spoke about the convenience of having such facilities within a stone's throw from where they live.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Some young parents told me part of the reason they bought a flat in this estate was predicated on the availability of childcare facilities in the neighbourhood.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: However, the number of places available at these childcare centres is limited due, in part, to high demand and also to the size of the centre.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Thus, some residents were disappointed to find out that despite having a childcare centre next door, enrolment is not a given.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Some residents shared that they even attempted to apply for a place for their children before these centres were completed or way before the centre opened their doors for registration, but were always met with a waiting list.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: In March 2015, the Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA) was reported to have said that the agency does monitor local demand and works closely with HDB on the issue of childcare places.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: It said, "the new estates with more young families, childcare centres are pre-built into new Build-To-Order (BTO) developments to cater to demand ahead of time".

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Thus, I would like to find out from the Ministry whether such demand is adequately met in new estates.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Furthermore, in the planning of such highly sought after facilities, could the Ministry ensure that residents living nearest to these childcare centres get some priority for admission?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: This arrangement should apply to anchor operators, especially since they are given subsidies and grants to operate childcare centres for the sole purpose of serving the new estate and the surrounding community.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: At this point, I would like to declare my interest as my wife has an interest in special needs childcare.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Chairman, these hikes hit the middle-income the hardest.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: It may also be a disincentive to some couples who may want to have more children.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: In 2015, I asked the Ministry if it would provide a breakdown of the cost components to justify fee hikes at childcare operators, but this was rejected.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Ironically, NTUC, which owns My First Skool, recently called for higher childcare subsidies to help middle-income parents.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: How does the Ministry check on the basis and justification of fee hikes, particularly from anchor operators who would benefit the most from economies of scale?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: At a time when Singaporeans are getting worried about the social divide between those who are better-off and those who are less advantaged, it is important for us to focus on core efforts that can help close this divide.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I trust we can all agree that quality education can be a social leveller.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Every child, regardless of his or her background, should have access to good education from a young age.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We know that ages between 0 to four years old are the most important years for development.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Therefore, I am happy to hear the Prime Minister's announcement at the National Day Rally last year about the Government's investments into early childhood education.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In recent years, we have made significant investments in this sector which has expanded so rapidly to cater to the needs of our young.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: To have quality preschool education, you need good infrastructure, good resources and, more importantly, good and sufficient teachers and other staff members.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: To make a difference to children not just academically but also emotionally and socially, our children deserve to have access to good education and resources that will provide the foundation on which they can pursue their dreams and passion in life.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: To enable every child to have a good start in life, the standards of preschool and preschool education have to be raised.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The passion and the skills of our preschool teachers will make a critical difference.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: What are the Ministry's plans to develop the early childhood profession?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This is because these centres meet many needs.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: First, the need of the mother who wishes to return to work to advance her career or supplement the household income together with her husband.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Second, the need of the child who will benefit from early childhood education.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And third, the need of the grandparents who will find time to rest when the child is at the childcare centre.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Therefore, in order to incentivise young couples to have more children, I have two suggestions.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: First, how can a larger amount of void deck space be allocated for childcare centres at the planning stage of new HDB BTO precincts?

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: (In Mandarin):   Although I graduated from an English medium school, the lessons that I learnt from young, songs by Feng Fei Fei and other songs that I listened to from the radio, Chinese novels that I read from libraries and the Chinese newspaper Sin Chew Jit Poh helped me fall in love with the Chinese language.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Today, young children receive good quality preschool education in their mother tongue language (MTL) starting from preschool.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In my work with the Education Services Union and the Committee to Promote Chinese Language Learning, I had the honour of witnessing the dedication and hard work of preschool Chinese teachers in cultivating love for the Chinese language amongst our children.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Besides enabling individuals to converse comfortably in their mother tongue for business and social interactions, it can also enhance understanding of our own culture.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I have met many parents who are also very supportive and believe that children should start learning how to use their mother tongue at childcare centres and homes to communicate.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: With the foundation that has been established, how can we do better going forward?

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Does MSF have an estimate of the number of MTL teachers we need in our preschools to meet future demands?

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What is the Ministry's strategy to attract and retain local MTL teachers?

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Will the Ministry consider giving greater support by providing teaching aids and tools for MTL preschool teachers, or inviting more education experts to share their expert knowledge and experience, so that MTL preschool teachers can have more resources to develop teaching materials containing localised content?

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Besides attracting more Singaporeans to join this profession through internship programmes, will the Minister consider launching more scholarship or bursary programmes targeted at preschool MTL teachers so as to identify, grow and nurture a pool of Singaporeans who are passionate about teaching MTL?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: One issue that deserves attention in our effort to preserve the Malay Language is the importance of cultivating interest among the young.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We are aware that the early years are important in our children's development.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Early education and exposure are important in order to develop their linguistic capabilities.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I am sure that this situation can be further improved to help mother tongue teachers in preschools.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Everyone born in this country is precious, and for more than economic reasons.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: In an effort to encourage Singaporeans to give birth to more, we must offer the assurance that their offspring would be valued, regardless of the condition they are born with.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: No one can guarantee that a child born to them is perfect.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Like you and I, people with special needs are sons and daughters of Singapore.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: They must be granted equal access to opportunities to partake in all aspects of society.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: In fact, neither can anyone guarantee that a typically developed person would not acquire any disability that comes with getting old or through an accident or mishap.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Including people with disabilities and other special needs among us, hence, is not doing charity.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Research in the past already showed a close link between disability and poverty for various reasons.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Unless there is effective and timely intervention, persons with special needs are likely to be unemployed, socially excluded and can encounter health issues earlier than others.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: For those who are more economically oriented, please know that the cost of supporting people with disabilities escalates when the latter are not educated, trained and supported effectively.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: In a rapidly disruptive age, such as now, people with special needs are clearly at risk of being left behind.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I have three questions I wish to seek clarification and make suggestions on.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: These are the roadmaps for Singapore to build a more inclusive society where persons with disabilities are empowered and enabled to realise their true potential.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: There are not many targets set, whether basic or stretched goals, and updates from the Ministry have been ad hoc.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I also ask for a tighter rein on its implementation by convening, for instance, an Execution Implementation Body comprising key strategic and hands-on leaders from the public, private and people sectors.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: This body should preferably be led by the highest authority in a coordinating Ministry like MSF, to ensure it has the muscle to influence and ensure the accountability by the various Government agencies and other stakeholders.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: New MSF Minister, or not so new, Desmond Lee, is known to be strong in such a coordinating role.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I have seen him in committees like this.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Two, on supporting and resourcing disability-specific enabling plans.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I had begun to encourage each major disability group to take ownership, to do a proper study and develop mini plans, so that the needs and gaps in their specific groups can be accurately defined, identified and addressed with outcomes and impact.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: However, the role of the Government is not diminished.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The Government has to take the lead to work much closer with the ground, meet them regularly and seriously nurture the ground.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: It can resource the ground in solutions that could already be working, or at risk of being terminated, and address genuine gaps in the landscape.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: For instance, NCSS had helped in the pilot of weekly respite programmes for families with more severely disabled adults with autism.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The staff from the Autism Association Singapore (AAS) where I volunteer, started a very successful pilot, providing much-needed respite to caregivers.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The programme, however, will not be financially supported after the pilot ends.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Some members from the deaf community have identified a high priority need for inclusive preschools, much like the Mayflower Primary School model that MOE has launched.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The preschool will provide the pipeline of students that will be more school-ready in the mainstream classrooms in Mayflower.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The take-up rate for employment is not as high as desired for this community.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: VWOs providing job training and employment services, together with SG Enable, will need a stronger listening ear from the Government and resourcing to expand their services so that more can work.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: There is a need to quickly create and nurture sheltered enterprises to support those who are more severe but can do lighter duty work.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I urge the Ministry to work closer with the ground to identify, support and resource disability-specific programmes surfaced by the ground.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: We do not want to go back to the dark ages more than a decade ago when students from special schools were forgotten when the anti-Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS) measures by MOE excluded them during that time.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: From the COS' announcements that I have listened to carefully this week, I believe that the public sector has not yet cultivated that habit of including this special group in their policy framing.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: There are great opportunities to ensure workforce inclusion and training, housing and digital equity through a digital literacy curriculum for special schools and so forth.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: I have worked with many public servants to know that many of them are supportive of the cause.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: But it is not yet a systemic habit.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: I, therefore, ask for an automatic checklist during policy formulation by every Government agency to ensure persons with special needs are always considered and included.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: Let them be elevated from being footnotes or after-thoughts.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: (In Mandarin):   The Enabling Masterplan 3 has been accepted by MSF for over a year.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: I would also like to ask the Minister if more Government agencies or private companies are willing to hire people with disabilities.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Are there any data to show the progress in this area?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Does the Government intend to take the lead in redesigning jobs so that people with disabilities can also make contributions at the public sector?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: I would also like to thank the Enabling Village for its efforts in this regard.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Not all the graduates from special needs schools are able to find a job or work.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: However, even if they cannot work, it does not mean that they have to be cooped up at home all day.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Therefore, I would like to ask the Minister whether there are any plans to strengthen the operations of adult centres for persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Chairman, I thank the Members for their continued support of my Ministry's work.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: (In Malay):   Over the past two weeks, Members have highlighted the importance of strengthening the foundations of our social harmony, even as we overcome the challenges ahead.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I am glad that the Budget this year seeks to support individuals and families to better prepare them for the future and care for one another.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: MSF strongly believes that families are critical institutions to enable a harmonious society.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We have always encouraged Singaporeans to make family life a priority.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Nonetheless, we recognise that the pressures of life can make it difficult for us to do so.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We have many policies aimed at easing these pressures, like parental leave provisions and parent support networks.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This is to ensure that we do not inadvertently sacrifice family for other demands.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: To better support young families in raising children, preschools play a key role.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We wish to ensure that every parent who wants a preschool place for their child will be able to have one.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This will give every child a good start in life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: To establish a strong bilingual foundation for our children early, and to give them exposure to their own customs and culture, we will also expand the provision of quality mother tongue teaching in preschools over the next five years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: There will be more MOE Kindergartens, which provide all three MTLs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The Government has been supporting more locals to become MTL preschool teachers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Since 2016, polytechnic students can pursue specialised MTL tracks.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Going forward, ECDA will work closely with the new National Institute of Early Childhood Development and other partners to enhance the training of MTL teachers and encourage more locals to take up MTL teaching in preschools.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: ECDA and MOE will also continue to work with sector partners to explore what other forms of professional support can be developed for our MTL teachers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Let us continue to work together and strengthen families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Let us work together to create a conducive environment for Singaporeans to start families and raise children, enjoy family life and build meaningful family ties.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Let this be our investment for a better society and a brighter future for all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: (In English):	With your permission, Sir, I would like to display two slides.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Over the past week, Members have highlighted the importance of strengthening the foundations of our social harmony despite the challenges ahead.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I am glad that the Budget seeks to support individuals and families to better prepare them for the future and care for one another.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: MSF strongly believes that families are critical institutions to enable a harmonious society.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Today, I shall talk about our roles in strengthening families, as well as in building a caring and inclusive society.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Mr Seah Kian Peng and Ms Tin Pei Ling expressed concerns about changing values and demographics, and if the family can continue to be the first line of support.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In the IPS Survey cited by Mr Seah Kian Peng, Ms Tin Pei Ling and Ms Rahayu Mahzam, respondents were asked to rank who should shoulder the main responsibility of taking care of our elderly, and 73% of the respondents ranked family first.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: After family, the Government was ranked second, and the community third.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Hence, Singaporeans do see family as the first line of support, but with the Government and community playing a major supporting role.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We will continue to encourage Singaporeans to make family life a priority, such as through the Families for Life Council, which champions family time.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We also have many policies, like parental leave provisions and parent support networks, to ensure that we do not sacrifice family for other demands.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We agree with Mr Christopher de Souza that preschools are key in meeting the needs of young families.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We wish to ensure that every parent who wants a preschool place for their child will be able to have one.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: This will give every child a good start in life.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Mr Png Eng Huat asked if we are providing enough preschool places for residents of new estates.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: ECDA has been working closely with HDB to build preschools as part of HDB BTO developments so that they can open earlier.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: To meet the preschool needs of residents, these new centres will have 200 places, twice the size of an average centre today.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We will continue to look at projects and watch supply and demand, and work closely with operators to establish childcare centres in areas of high demand.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Where there are areas with high demand, we will continue to build.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: ECDA has also been working with the Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) to ensure that developers set aside space for preschools in private residential sites released through the Government Land Sales programme.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Mr Desmond Choo asked how we will ensure that preschool and student care remain affordable.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Mr Pritam Singh also asked how we review fees for preschool operators.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Similarly, we will continue to monitor the affordability of student care for the lower-income families.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: They raise fees periodically to keep up with increases in operating costs, and to recruit and retain teachers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: While ECDA does not regulate fees charged by these operators, it requires centres to report fee increases and give parents at least four months’ notice.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Centres need to explain the basis for the increase and directly engage parents who face difficulties in meeting the new amount.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In addition, Anchor Operators and Partner Operators are subjected to fee caps.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: For other preschool operators, fees are adjusted to keep pace with manpower and operating costs, as well as quality enhancements.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Together with MOE Kindergartens, these Government-supported preschools provide affordable, quality services for almost half of all preschoolers, and have stabilised industry median fees.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: By 2020, we will require 20,000 early childhood professionals, 3,000 more than today.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam and Mr Desmond Choo asked how this growth can be supported amidst a tight manpower situation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: There are three key strategies under the ITM.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: First, we will develop more efficient, innovative services for parents and children.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: For example, infants and toddlers currently have separate spaces within the same centre.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: These spaces could be shared, so that children can transit more smoothly from the infant to toddler age group.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Operators can also enroll more children, while maintaining standards of quality and safety.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Second, we will introduce solutions to free up teachers’ time for higher-value work, such as lesson planning.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Administrative responsibilities will be simplified through centralised services and use of technology.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Third, we will expand the opportunities for more people to join the early childhood sector.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Beyond academic qualifications, there are many persons with aptitude and competence to join the sector.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: One job role we have piloted is Allied Infant Educarers, who receive on-the-job coaching and supervision to care for babies.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: To complement the ITM, we will do more to support our early childhood professionals.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Enrolment in early childhood diploma courses has doubled since 2015.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Early childhood professionals have also enjoyed higher salaries and more professional development.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Mr Amrin Amin asked about plans to further develop the profession.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The AOPs will take the lead to develop career progression opportunities for their teachers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: This is possible because our AOPs have grown in scale and diversity of operations.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: These leadership roles include managing a larger centre or a cluster of centres or mentoring junior teachers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: To support this, the AOPs will provide more structured leadership development.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: These efforts will raise the quality of our preschools.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Under the guidance of her principal then, she developed her skills and attended professional development courses.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: She then became a senior teacher and honed her leadership skills by mentoring trainee teachers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Due to her strong performance, Amanda has been promoted to Acting Principal of My First Skool @ Senja.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: It is now her turn to provide her teachers with opportunities to grow and develop.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: There are many resources to tap on, such as the Professional Development Programmes under ECDA.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I would also like to encourage operators to recognise the growing contributions of their staff and remunerate them based on their job responsibilities, competencies and performance.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: This way, they will be able to retain good teachers with passion, and raise career prospects across the whole sector.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam asked how we can better support quality bilingual education in preschools.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Mr Ang Hin Kee also asked how we can attract and retain sufficient MTL teachers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I agree that MTL is important and, when it comes to language, starting early helps.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Over the next five years, parents can look forward to more MTL exposure in preschools.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: There will be more MOE Kindergartens which provide all three MTLs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Today, all AOP preschools already provide Chinese lessons.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The Government has been supporting more locals to become MTL preschool teachers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Since 2016, polytechnic students can pursue specialised MTL tracks.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: These efforts have increased the pool of local MTL preschool teachers to 3,300 in 2017, 35% more than in 2015.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Going forward, ECDA will work closely with the new National Institute of Early Childhood Development and other partners to enhance the training of MTL teachers and encourage more locals to teach MTL in preschools.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Teaching resources, such as the Nurturing Early Learners, or NEL Framework for MTL, Educators' Guide and NEL Big Books for MTL have also been shared with the sector.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: One beneficiary of these resources is Ms Nabilah Binte Abdul Fitrey from PAP Community Foundation (PCF) Sparkletots Preschool @ Bukit Batok.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Ms Nabilah used to teach English but switched to teaching Malay in 2017 when the centre decided to provide Malay lessons.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: She has found the NEL resources for MTL useful.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Through teaching Malay, she hopes for her children to learn about the customs of their culture and establish a strong bilingual foundation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: ECDA and MOE will continue to work together with sector partners to explore what other forms of professional support can be developed for our MTL teachers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: To Mr Ang Hin Kee, wo men hui jing li er wei (我们会尽力而为).

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: To Ms Rahayu Mahzam, kami akan melakukan yang terbaik.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: All these mean we will do our best.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Besides investing in our future generation, we should also care for the generation before us, our seniors.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: They have a wealth of skills and experiences and continue to contribute to our communities and families.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: But we acknowledge that it may not be easy to manage the deepening demands of caregiving.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Mr Kok Heng Leun suggested at the Ministry of Manpower's (MOM's) COS to provide allowances to caregivers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Currently, caregivers may tap on the Caregiver Training Grant which provides $200 for the caregiving training courses each year.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: They also benefit from tax reliefs and a lower foreign domestic worker (FDW) levy.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Hence, our approach is to help to defray costs to families caring for their seniors and loved ones.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We will continue to review how we can provide more support for caregivers, including respite care options at Senior Care Centres and Adult Disability Homes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We also thank Mr Chen Show Mao for his suggestions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We will study all ideas raised by him and other Members as well.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In addition, MSF works to ensure that we are adequately prepared if our loved ones lose mental capacity.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Beyond our seniors, we encourage Singaporeans, especially our middle-aged population, to plan ahead by making an LPA.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We have made it much more convenient and affordable to do so, by simplifying the application process and waiving the application fee.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Ms Sylvia Lim asked if the OPG is able to cope with the workload.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Although the surge in applications has led to a longer processing time, we have already streamlined processes and hired more staff.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I wish to assure the public that the longer processing time does not affect them adversely, as the LPA application will still remain valid.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We will also introduce a new online LPA system by 2021, which should cut down processing time.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The increased workload in LPA registration does not affect the supervision and investigation functions of the OPG, as it is done by a separate team of officers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Ms Sylvia Lim also asked about the reasons for the revocation of LPAs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: This could occur due to events, such as the donor’s or donee’s death, or the donee’s loss of mental capacity.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I will now speak on persons with disabilities and their families.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Ms Denise Phua and Mr Ang Wei Neng asked about the progress of the 3rd Enabling Masterplan (EMP3).

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Over the past year, we have enhanced training and employment opportunities for persons with disabilities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Under the Hospital-to-Work programme, SG Enable and the Society for the Physically Disabled (SPD) have extended assistance to persons with acquired disabilities by supporting their return to work through reskilling, goalsetting and rehabilitation through therapy.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We have also extended the School-to-Work programme to more schools.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: It provides counselling, soft skills training and work trial opportunities for students in special education (SPED) schools before they are matched with suitable jobs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Mr Ang Wei Neng asked if employers are becoming more receptive to employing persons with disabilities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: SG Enable works closely with employers to help them build an inclusive company culture and redesign jobs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: More employees with disabilities have also been hired in the private sector.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: To defray transport costs, we also enhanced the Taxi Subsidy Scheme to benefit more persons with disabilities, including those attending employment-related training supported by SG Enable.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Ms Denise Phua asked if MSF could set up a committee to involve the community more in the implementation of EMP3.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: MSF chairs an interagency committee which collaborates with the people and private sectors to implement the EMP3 recommendations.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Community groups are closely involved in various work areas, and we will continue to approach the community for feedback, ideas and partnership in EMP3 initiatives.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: To facilitate community-driven ground-up initiatives, we have also created several channels to provide for funding support.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As we strengthen support for persons with disabilities, let us not forget their caregivers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The role of a caregiver is critical but challenging, and more support will be provided to caregivers of persons with disabilities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: SG Enable today supports caregivers in their care role.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: This includes the information and referral to disability services provided through the SG Enable Infoline and the concierge at the Enabling Village.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Moving ahead, SG Enable will further work with public sector agencies and community partners to equip caregivers with information and advice to build up their self-care and caregiving skills.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: It will also partner VWOs to improve caregiver support, especially at critical transition points of the care recipient’s life.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: There is much to be gained from the support and solidarity of fellow caregivers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: To facilitate this, SG Enable will be setting up a Caregivers' Space at the Enabling Village by the end of the year.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: It will serve as a place for activities organised by peer support groups, as well as caregiver training and engagement by VWOs and community partners.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We want caregivers to come, learn from the experiences of fellow caregivers, and get advice and moral support as they walk their caregiving journey.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: This will strengthen the network of support for caregivers, which Mr Desmond Choo spoke about.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Mr Desmond Choo also highlighted the importance of respite care in improving caregivers’ well-being.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Ample respite care services are provided at seven Adult Disability Homes and three Children Disability Homes supported by means-tested subsidies of up to 75%.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: With more caregivers remaining in the workforce, the demand for day care may grow, as Mr Ang Wei Neng noted.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We will add another 200 Day Activity Centre places this year for adults with disabilities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We are also building up the centres' capabilities to support persons with moderate-to-severe needs with quality programming and intervention services.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Another issue that preoccupies caregivers is the care of their loved ones with disabilities upon their death.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Caregivers will be better supported with care and financial planning for their dependants.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The Special Needs Trust Company (SNTC) is a non-profit trust company which provides subsidised trust services.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: It has served more than 500 families since its inception 10 years ago.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: One family that benefited from its service is the Yaps.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Mr Yap and his son Hon Wee, who has cerebral palsy, live in a rental flat.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Mr Yap was diagnosed with cancer last year and worries about Hon Wee’s long-term care needs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As he has no other familial support, Mr Yap approached SNTC to set up a trust for his son.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Now, Mr Yap is assured that if his son outlives him, his savings, including CPF monies, will be safeguarded, invested and paid out according to a care plan customised to meet Hon Wee’s needs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Many more caregivers of loved ones with disabilities can benefit from such peace of mind.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: SNTC will be stepping up its outreach to caregivers to raise awareness on the care planning and financial education available to them.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We will also enhance the application processes to schemes and services that support caregivers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As Mr Murali previously highlighted, persons with cognitive disabilities sometimes face difficulties in being assessed for schemes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Their caregivers will soon be able to apply for the FDW levy concession and grant with greater ease.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: MSF has worked with MOH to include MSF’s Client Assessment Form (CAF) as an alternative tool to evaluate the level of support a person requires to pursue activities of daily living, to support applications for the FDW levy concession and grant.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We will also strengthen the last mile of support, ensuring that caregivers know about our services and can access them conveniently.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We will work with other agencies to explore equipping more frontline officers, including those from SGO, with knowledge about disability-related schemes and services.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Chairman, my Ministry is committed to strengthening families and building a more inclusive society.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: However, we are only one piece of the puzzle.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: This endeavour requires the combined efforts from all of us – Government agencies, businesses, community organisations and, indeed, every Singaporean, including all of us here.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Let us continue to work together to make Singapore a great place for families and an inclusive home for all Singaporeans.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: This will be our investment for a better society and a better future for all of us.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Members for their valuable thoughts and comments.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Our work at MSF covers a broad range of complex issues, like strengthening families, providing social safety nets, giving children from all backgrounds a good start, enabling people with disabilities and special needs, as well as protecting the vulnerable amongst us.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: One area of our work is to tackle the challenge of income inequality.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is part of concerted and coordinated efforts among Government Ministries to ensure social harmony for Singaporeans, as highlighted by the Prime Minister recently.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Over the years, we have put in place support schemes and networks on the ground.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This has ensured broad-based social uplifting through employment, sustained income growth, and universal access to education, housing and healthcare.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These mutually reinforcing economic and social policies have been at the core of our success in strengthening our social compact and moving the whole of society forward.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Most Members of this House would have had this experience of visiting the modest homes of our seniors.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Because of a lack of opportunity in the early years, they had lower educational qualifications, but worked hard for many decades, often in lower paying jobs, such as factory workers, cleaners or hawkers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: On the walls of their flat, however, would usually be a family portrait taking pride of place.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Their children would often be seen wearing mortar boards and graduation gowns.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They would have done better in life, because of the broader opportunities they had, which their parents had not.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I met one such couple, an elderly Indian couple, who worked in low wage jobs before retiring.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: One of their sons was sent by his company to head their operations overseas, while the other two are professionals.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Social uplifting for this family and others took a single generation.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Recently, I met some families that used to get financial help and bursaries for their children.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For various reasons, these middle-aged parents did not do so well when they were growing up, and needed help with arrears, health problems and unemployment.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Their parents were low-income, and they, too, remained low-income.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But they have since stopped approaching social service agencies for help, because their children have recently graduated from university, polytechnic or ITE, and found good jobs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For these families, it took yet another generation.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, our broad-based policies continue to keep the engine of social mobility strong.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Having said that, as society develops, it tends to settle and stratify and those who remain at the lower end of the income spectrum face the risk of remaining there, for a variety of intractable reasons – health, disability, family problems, incarceration, addiction, unemployment and many other reasons.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And because of economic and technological disruption picking up pace, families that have been doing well all along may suddenly find themselves in dire straits, for example, because the main breadwinner has been made redundant or been retrenched.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: What this means is that we must focus even harder on targeted interventions, over and beyond our broad-based social policies.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Members asked about MSF’s specific role in tackling this issue.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have made deliberate moves to strengthen social mobility by providing early, upstream support and more targeted assistance to lower-income Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Education has been key in the Government’s efforts to improve social mobility.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: MSF's touchpoint starts much earlier, before the formal schooling years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As shared by my colleague Senior Parliamentary Secretary Faishal Ibrahim, we will continue to expand the provision of affordable, accessible and quality preschool places, so that every child can have a good start in life.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Early feedback on KidSTART's impact on child outcomes has been promising.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have also steadily strengthened our social support system.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And as I shared in my opening speech, we are continuously seeking to improve our schemes and social service delivery, so that we can maximise the impact of social services and community resources.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Our other recent initiatives are in the same spirit, involving stronger collaboration with other agencies and VWOs and listening even more actively and intently to the community.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have also set up a Youth Advisory Group, comprising 12 young people, some of whom have been through very, very difficult times, to help us review and test our policy ideas and better implement policies and programmes, so as to reach out to vulnerable youths at-risk.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: To support vulnerable seniors with multiple or complex needs and facilitate planning, SSOs will continue to work closely with AIC and other community agencies to strengthen CNS.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Some VWOs I spoke to highlighted the importance of upstream preventive work that could enable us to identify and intervene at the start, where families or individuals show signs of need.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will work closely with them to do so.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Seah Kian Peng rightly pointed out that our shared values lie at the heart of our social compact.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Our policies to improve social mobility are motivated by our conviction to build a Singapore where all of us can lead lives with dignity and meaning and participate and contribute in our own ways.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is not only about enabling personal responsibility, but about society collectively stepping in to play a part.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: At the National Day Rally in 2013, the Prime Minister articulated the new way forward, where the community and Government do more to support individuals, especially vulnerable groups, like the low-income, elderly and persons with disabilities.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will continue to support individuals to be self-reliant.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is where we do not just provide a safety net, but a trampoline to help people to bounce back up, where possible.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This requires a whole network of support to break the cycles that have led to the situation.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It is not just about referring and providing someone in need with the right assistance but, more importantly, about showing empathy to fellow Singaporeans and banding around to lend support.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Collective responsibility and personal responsibility are not trade-offs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The community and the Government doing more does not mean that individuals are disempowered to play their part.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: If we each put in our bit and work together, we reinforce one another and multiply our ability to tackle challenges manifold.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, we must continue to make space for the community to contribute, alongside the Government, to help those who need help to regain their footing.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And as we do so, we must be careful not to erode the dignity and resolve of individuals in wanting to improve their own and their family's lives.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Chairman, I would now like to say a few words in Mandarin.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: (In Mandarin):   Parliamentary colleagues, one of the top priorities of our Ministry is to look into building a caring and inclusive society.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Over the last few years, we have invested a lot of resources and explored new ways to ensure that our social support system is better able to satisfy the needs of our people.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Looking forward, our Ministry will focus on studying ways to uphold our people-centric principle to further enhance the coordination and collaboration of organisations providing assistance in order to offer more comprehensive assistance to those in need.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We strive to provide simple and convenient one-stop assistance to all those who seek help so that they can receive timely assistance to regain their footing.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For applicants who apply for assistance at social service agencies, they will have easier access to basic information on various assistance schemes and will be referred for the necessary services.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Social service agencies will also further simplify the application procedures for various assistance schemes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This includes sharing the information of those who seek help so that they do not have to repeat their stories over and over again to the various agencies or to fill in the same information repeatedly.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I believe that with better coordination and collaboration among agencies, Singaporeans facing difficulties will then be able to better get the help they need.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: She is a single mother who lives with her two sons and aged divorced parents.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: She is unable to work as she needs to go for regular treatment due to illness and, unfortunately, both her children also have medical conditions.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Furthermore, her aged mother likes to hoard things in the house.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, besides financial assistance, she also needs help to clean the house and improve her living condition.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The SSO @ Woodlands thus worked together with HDB, Fei Yue Family Service Centre, medical social workers, the school and the PA's grassroots organisations to come up with solutions for her entire family.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They helped Mdm Cheok to apply for financial assistance, and are providing long-term counselling for the family.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They also helped to clean up her house.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Her 16-year-old younger son has started classes at ITE, and her 26-year-old elder son has started an ad hoc job.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This proves that as long as there is good coordination and good collaboration, we would be able to help Singaporeans in need more comprehensively, so that every one of us can be self-reliant and enjoy a better life.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: (In English): Mr Chairman, this whole-of-society approach runs through MSF's continued efforts to improve outcomes for vulnerable and at-risk groups.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This includes our work on children and young persons, and even individuals who sleep rough in the open.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Our approach towards youth offenders is premised on gradated intervention.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Where possible, we do not want youths to enter the criminal justice system.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Where suitable, youths are referred to attend diversionary programmes to address the risk of re-offending.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Nonetheless, some youths may require firmer intervention when the offence is more serious, or when family support is unavailable.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These youths would tend to be heard by the Community Court, which adopts a more restorative and rehabilitative approach, compared to the adult Courts.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Our aim remains the same – to ensure youth offenders in Singapore receive appropriate help to reintegrate into society.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Murali Pillai suggested for the CYPA to protect children beyond serious physical harm, including children with persistent school absenteeism issues.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Irregular or non-school attendance can be a manifestation of complex underlying family issues, such as marital, financial or health challenges.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Statutory intervention and legal enforcement cannot be the only or "go-to" approach.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The use of legislative levers is insufficient on its own.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, our approach must continue to be to work with community partners to provide a range of help options to holistically and sustainably address the family’s needs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As to Mr Murali Pillai's specific case that he is dealing with, we will support the work of partners on the ground to solve the case.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Another issue that will benefit from Government-community partnership is rough sleeping or homelessness.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Dr Lily Neo asked if we could reduce the number of Singaporeans sleeping rough in the open, and about the available shelter options for them.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is a segment of the cases we encounter, where persons sleep in public places, instead of returning to their homes due to – as the Member says – family conflicts, disputes with co-tenants, cluttered homes, and many other reasons.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Sleeping in the rough puts their welfare, health and safety at risk, and also impacts the immediate neighbourhood.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: MSF officers regularly engage persons sleeping rough in Chinatown and other locations to provide assistance that may be needed to address the challenges they face.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We need a more coordinated, whole-of-society approach to address the underlying issues and needs of these individuals.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: MSF works closely with other frontline agencies and the community to reach out and coordinate the help that they need.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This may include admission to a shelter, financial assistance or counselling for social or family issues, or for us to work to with MOM to give their employers a call, if they are foreigners, for instance, are sleeping rough to be close to their workplaces.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: MSF has also established referral protocols and platforms among SSOs, FSCs and HDB to assist persons facing complex social and housing issues.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We can do more and will continue to strengthen interagency coordination and information sharing to enable clients to secure stable housing.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For those who are work-capable, the Welfare Homes will work towards reintegrating them into the community.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: During their stay, the individuals can continue to work or receive assistance to seek employment and access social services and other assistance to address their needs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are blessed that there are community groups which are reaching out actively to befriend these individuals and encourage them to seek assistance.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have been engaging these groups to see how we can work even more closely together and welcome more to partner us on this journey forward.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Members of the community can also play their part by looking out for those in need and rendering assistance or referring them to us in MSF.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Chairman, I now move on to speak about the social service sector.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The sector and those who work in it are vital and indispensable partners in our mission to tackle income inequality, uplift families and individuals, protect the vulnerable, and ensure that no one is left behind.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As I hear more about the work that social service professionals do each and every day, I am humbled and inspired by the deep care and concern they show towards fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But the social service sector is not immune to the challenges that affect other sectors – an ageing workforce, slowing workforce growth and the need to upgrade skills and innovate work processes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
